# 3D

This is the short version. The 3D library is `bevy` (`raea guide bevy`): it routes to one file per topic (scene and
camera, lights, materials, meshes, animation, 3D games, models and pictures, bloom and fog, limits), each with a
working example. Read it as soon as a piece needs more than a turning shape under two lights.

## What to do

- The 3D names are Bevy's, each from its Bevy module: `Camera3d` (`raea/camera`), `Transform` and `Quat`
  (`raea/transform`), `Mesh3d` and the shapes (`raea/mesh`), `StandardMaterial` (`raea/pbr`), the lights
  (`raea/light`). Write the scene straight in your tree, inside a full-frame `AbsoluteFill`; no wrapper is needed.
  The 3D is drawn under the page, so 2D parts (titles, captions) can sit over it in the same composition.
- Build the scene from:
  - `<Camera3d transform={Transform.fromXyz(0, 1, 6).lookingAt([0, 0, 0])} projection={{ Perspective: { fov:
    (50 * Math.PI) / 180 } }} />`: the fov is vertical, in radians;
  - `<AmbientLight brightness color>` (cd/m², 80-200) and `<DirectionalLight transform illuminance color
    shadow_maps_enabled>` (lux, 8,000-12,000 for daylight), the sun shining along its transform's -Z, so give it
    `.lookingAt([0, 0, 0])`;
  - `<Mesh3d transform>`, holding one shape and one `<StandardMaterial base_color emissive metallic
    perceptual_roughness>`. The shapes are `<Cuboid half_size={[w / 2, h / 2, d / 2]} />`, `<Sphere radius />`,
    `<Plane3d normal half_size />`, `<Cylinder radius half_height />` and `<Torus major_radius minor_radius />`.
    For a cartoon look use `<ToonMaterial base_color steps={2} outline={{ width: 3 }} />` instead (hard light bands
    and an ink line; inside a `<Model>` it tones the model's own materials); `raea guide bevy/materials` has it.
- Animate a mesh by computing its transform from the frame, exactly as you would a 2D part:
  `Transform.fromXyz(x, y, z).withRotation(Quat.fromEuler("XYZ", rx, ry, rz)).withScale(s)`. **Rotation is in
  radians.**
- Or declare a mesh's motion once: `<Mesh3d animate={{ y: track({ 0: 3, 18: 0 }, curve.spring({ damping: 12 })),
  rotateY: track({ 0: 0, 59: Math.PI }, "in-out-sine") }}>`. `x`, `y`, `z` set its translation, `rotateX`,
  `rotateY`, `rotate` its rotation in radians, and `scale` its size. The engine samples it from the frame
  (motion/animating has the tracks and curves). A material's colour and glow are per-frame values: compute them
  from the frame.
- Model shapes the primitives can't make with Manifold solids: `manifold.box(w, h, d)`, `roundedBox`, `sphere`,
  `cylinder(r, h)` (along z), `cone`, `torus` and `text3d(text, size, depth, font, weight)`, combined with
  `.union()`, `.minus()`, `.intersect()` and `.hull()` and moved with `.move()`, `.rotate()` (**in degrees**) and
  `.scale()`. Pass the result as `<Mesh3d shape={solid}>`. You can also ask a solid about itself with `volume()`,
  `bounds()` and `slice(z)`.
- Colour materials from the brand kit. A material's `base_color` is a plain string handed to the 3D renderer, so read it
  from `brand.json` (`kit.palette.accent`) rather than typing a hex. The element that holds the camera has its
  background cleared to show the scene, and its colour becomes the scene's clear colour.
- For a scene with many moving things, keep them in an ECS world (`raea/ecs`) and draw it with `<Scene
  world>`. It draws the world's `mesh`, `camera`, `light` and `ambient` entities at the current frame (`motion/games`).

## Why

3D elements render as plain elements that carry their props, which raea's engine turns into camera, light and mesh
entities and draws with Bevy. A mesh's geometry reaches the renderer as a Manifold expression (`box(1, 2, 3)`), so a
modelled solid and a primitive travel the same way and render the same frames.

Manifold solids are made by the engine when it renders. Check a scene built from solids by rendering it and looking
at a still.

## Common mistakes

- `Quat.fromEuler("XYZ", 0, 45, 0)` meaning degrees. A transform's rotation is radians: `Math.PI / 4`. (Solid's
  `.rotate()` is degrees, so the two differ.)
- A Mesh3d with two shapes or no material. Give it one of each.
- `metallic` or `perceptual_roughness` outside [0, 1], or a scale of 0: they throw. A `fov` of 40 is radians, a
  fisheye: write `(40 * Math.PI) / 180`.
- `color="var(--brand-accent)"` on a material. The 3D renderer doesn't read CSS. Use the kit's hex from brand.json.
- A hex colour typed into a material. Read it from the kit.
- Rebuilding the same solid on every frame. Build it once at module level (in the engine) and move the Mesh3d.

## Example: a turning product block with the title over it

```tsx
import { AbsoluteFill, Composition, Easing, interpolate, registerRoot, useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig } from "raea";
import { Torus } from "raea/3d";
import { Camera3d } from "raea/camera";
import { css } from "./styles.gen";
import kit from "./brand/brand.json";
import { LinearRgba, Srgba } from "raea/color";
import { StandardMaterial } from "raea/pbr";
import { Cuboid, Mesh3d } from "raea/mesh";
import { Quat, Transform } from "raea/transform";
import { AmbientLight, DirectionalLight } from "raea/light";

const OUT = Easing.out(Easing.cubic);
const ACCENT = kit.palette.accent ?? kit.colors[0].hex;
const SURFACE = kit.palette.surface ?? kit.colors[0].hex;

export default function Turn() {
  const f = useCurrentFrame();
  const { fps } = useVideoConfig();
  const spin = (f / fps) * (Math.PI / 2); // a quarter turn a second
  const drop = interpolate(f, [0, 18], [3, 0], { easing: OUT, extrapolateLeft: "clamp", extrapolateRight: "clamp" });
  return (
    <AbsoluteFill style={{ backgroundColor: "var(--brand-background)" }}>
      <style>{css}</style>
      <AbsoluteFill>
        <Camera3d transform={Transform.fromXyz(0, 1.2, 6).lookingAt([0, 0, 0])} projection={{ Perspective: { fov: (40 * Math.PI) / 180 } }} />
        <AmbientLight brightness={160} />
        <DirectionalLight transform={Transform.fromXyz(3, 5, 4).lookingAt([0, 0, 0])} illuminance={12800} shadow_maps_enabled />
        <Mesh3d transform={Transform.fromXyz(0, drop, 0).withRotation(Quat.fromEuler("XYZ", 0.2, spin, 0))}>
          <Cuboid half_size={[0.8, 0.8, 0.8]} />
          <StandardMaterial base_color={ACCENT} perceptual_roughness={0.35} metallic={0.1} />
        </Mesh3d>
        <Mesh3d transform={Transform.fromXyz(0, -1.4, 0).withRotation(Quat.fromEuler("XYZ", Math.PI / 2, 0, 0))}>
          <Torus major_radius={1.8} minor_radius={0.05} />
          <StandardMaterial base_color={SURFACE} perceptual_roughness={0.5} emissive={LinearRgba.from(Srgba.hex(ACCENT)).mul(0.6)} />
        </Mesh3d>
      </AbsoluteFill>
      <div style={{ position: "absolute", left: 90, right: 90, top: 300, textAlign: "center", fontFamily: "var(--brand-font-heading)", fontWeight: 800, fontSize: 120, lineHeight: 1, color: "var(--brand-text)" }}>
        Built to last
      </div>
    </AbsoluteFill>
  );
}

registerRoot(() => <Composition id="turn" component={Turn} width={1080} height={1920} fps={30} durationInFrames={120} />);
```

## Example: a modelled solid (engine only)

```tsx
import { AbsoluteFill, Composition, registerRoot, useCurrentFrame } from "raea";
import { manifold, type Solid } from "raea/3d";
import { Camera3d } from "raea/camera";
import { css } from "./styles.gen";
import kit from "./brand/brand.json";
import { StandardMaterial } from "raea/pbr";
import { Mesh3d } from "raea/mesh";
import { Quat, Transform } from "raea/transform";
import { AmbientLight, DirectionalLight } from "raea/light";

/** A rounded tile with a hole through it, built once (the engine holds it). */
let tile: Solid | null = null;
function getTile(): Solid {
  tile ??= manifold.roundedBox(2, 2, 0.4, 0.15).minus(manifold.cylinder(0.45, 1));
  return tile;
}

export default function Tile() {
  const f = useCurrentFrame();
  return (
    <AbsoluteFill style={{ backgroundColor: "var(--brand-background)" }}>
      <style>{css}</style>
      <Camera3d transform={Transform.fromXyz(0, 0, 6)} projection={{ Perspective: { fov: (40 * Math.PI) / 180 } }} />
      <AmbientLight brightness={200} />
      <DirectionalLight transform={Transform.fromXyz(2, 4, 5).lookingAt([0, 0, 0])} illuminance={11200} shadow_maps_enabled />
      <Mesh3d transform={Transform.IDENTITY.withRotation(Quat.fromEuler("XYZ", 0.3, f * 0.03, 0))} shape={getTile()}>
        <StandardMaterial base_color={kit.palette.accent ?? kit.colors[0].hex} perceptual_roughness={0.4} />
      </Mesh3d>
    </AbsoluteFill>
  );
}

registerRoot(() => <Composition id="tile" component={Tile} width={1080} height={1080} fps={30} durationInFrames={90} />);
```
